pr_title: Feature: Added a prompt when failing to rename items requiring additional permissions
pr_body:
**Resolved / Related Issues**
- [x] Were these changes approved in an issue or discussion with the project maintainers? In order to prevent extra work, feature requests and changes to the codebase must be approved before the pull request will be reviewed. This prevents extra work for the contributors and maintainers.
   Closes #8326 

**Known bugs**
- There are two cases where `Edit permissions` doesn't work:
  1. You start to rename an item on one page, and then (somehow) navigate to another before clicking `Edit permissions`
  2. You open the properties window for that item, navigate to a different page and then rename it

The issue behind these bugs is that the `Properties` window depends on `IShellPage` and `ListedItem`, while `RenameAsync` doesn't. To get those values, I'm using `ContentPageContext`, but this doesn't work if you change the working directory while renaming. Do you have any ideas on how I can fix this without messing up the code too much?

issue_context.title: Bug: No warning is shown when failing to rename files as non admin
issue_context.body:
### Description

No under permission warnings are shown when renaming Utilman.exe to Utilman2.exe under system32

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Go to system32
2. find Utilman.exe
2. Rename it to Utilman2.exe
3. Select "Yes" for UAC
4. Nothing changed.

### Expected behavior

There is no rename failure message. Normally it should tell us to get permission from TrustedInstaller

### Files Version

Version: 2.1.13.0

### Windows Version

Windows 11 Dev 22543.1000

### Relevant Assets/Logs

[debug_fulltrust.log](https://github.com/files-community/Files/files/8054901/debug_fulltrust.log)
[debug.log](https://github.com/files-community/Files/files/8054902/debug.log)

2022-02-13
comments: This should be merged with #13229 as it's an issue related to administrator permissions.
There wasn't support for renaming in the initial PR. So I don't think it should be merged.
@gave92 is this addressed or was that only for copy and delete?
This issue is different. This is about showing an error for files you can't rename even as administrator (this dialog from FE)

How detailed should the dialog be?
![image](https://github.com/files-community/Files/assets/102259289/60178cf9-1e86-4a82-bd38-c918ef5005e5)
Is something like this okay? Should we add any other info?

Title: "Failed to rename item"
Content: "Editing `path` requires permission from TrustedInstaller."
Primary action: "OK"
Secondary action: "Edit permissions"

> Secondary action: "Edit permissions"

Should this action open the `Advanced Security` tab in the `Properties` window?
Opening the regular security page is probably easier.
